<thought>We need the number of chemically equivalent hydrogen atoms (unique proton environments) in the compound. The tool `proton_nmr_spectra` returns the 1H NMR spectrum for the target compound (the SMILES is implicitly known from the task). We'll call it to obtain the spectrum, then count the distinct signals (peaks) reported, which correspond to unique hydrogen environments.</thought>
